answer: An organization can discover devices connected to its network without actively probing them by utilizing an active discovery tool, as specified in Control 1: Inventory and Control of Enterprise Assets [S1]. The tool should be configured to execute daily, or more frequently, to identify assets connected to the enterprise's network [S1]. This safeguard is part of the CIS Controls v8.1.2 [S1].

The safeguard that uses application allowlisting to prevent unauthorized software from executing is Safeguard 2.5 - Allowlist Authorized Software [S1]. This safeguard instructs to use technical controls, such as application allowlisting, to ensure only authorized software can execute or be accessed [S1]. The safeguard also requires reassessment bi-annually, or more frequently [S1].

Sensitive data should not be processed on enterprise assets intended for lower-sensitivity data [S1]. Data should be segmented based on its sensitivity for processing and storage [S1]. This ensures that sensitive data is not inadvertently exposed to unauthorized access [S1].

Record the owner, purpose, and review date for non-human accounts in the inventory, as required by Control 5: Account Management and Safeguard 5.5 [S1]. The inventory must contain department owner, review date, and purpose for service accounts [S1]. Perform service account reviews to validate that all active accounts are authorized, on a recurring schedule at a minimum quarterly, or more frequently [S1].

Establish and maintain an inventory of the enterprise’s authentication and authorization systems, including those hosted on-site or at a remote service provider [S1]. Review and update the inventory, at a minimum, annually, or more frequently [S1]. This safeguard directly matches the question, as it specifically mentions systems hosted locally and by remote service providers [S1].

Address software vulnerabilities by establishing and maintaining a process to accept and address reports, including providing a means for external entities to report, and updating documentation annually or when significant enterprise changes occur [S2]. This process should include a vulnerability handling policy, responsible party, and a process for intake, assignment, remediation, and remediation testing [S2]. The process should also utilize a vulnerability tracking system with severity ratings and metrics [S2].

Safeguard 8.5 requires audit logs to include details such as event source, username, timestamp, and network addresses [S1]. The specific details required include event source, date, username, timestamp, source addresses, destination addresses, and other useful elements [S1]. This safeguard is part of Control 8: Audit Log Management [S1].

Enforce and update network-based URL filters to limit enterprise assets from connecting to potentially malicious or unapproved websites, using category-based filtering, reputation-based filtering, or block lists [S1]. Enforce filters for all enterprise assets [S1]. This can be achieved by maintaining and enforcing network-based URL filters [S1].

Enable anti-exploitation features on enterprise assets and software, such as Microsoft Data Execution Prevention (DEP), Windows Defender Exploit Guard (WDEG), or Apple System Integrity Protection (SIP) and Gatekeeper, is safeguard 10.5 [S1].

An organization should test a sample of its backups quarterly, or more frequently, for a sampling of in-scope enterprise assets [S1]. This is specified in safeguard 11.5 - Test Data Recovery [S1]. The frequency of testing is not further defined in the provided evidence [S1].

Safeguard 12.8 requires separate computing resources for administrative tasks, either physically or logically separated, for all administrative tasks or tasks requiring administrative access [S1]. This safeguard is part of Control 12: Network Infrastructure Management [S1]. The computing resources should be segmented from the enterprise's primary network and not be allowed internet access [S1].

A network traffic monitoring system monitors network traffic for signs of intrusion, rather than running on individual hosts, as part of the Network Monitoring and Defense control [S1]. This is achieved by deploying a network-based intrusion detection solution, which is the opposite of deploying a host-based intrusion detection solution on individual hosts [S1]. Train workforce on how to identify and report missing software updates or failures in automated patching, including notifying IT personnel of any failures in automated processes and tools [S1]. This training is part of Control 14: Security Awareness and Skills Training [S1]. The training should include verifying and reporting out-of-date software patches or any failures in automated processes and tools [S1].

Suppliers should be grouped according to factors such as data sensitivity, data volume, and availability requirements, as these characteristics are considered in the classification of service providers [S1]. Classification consideration may include one or more characteristics, such as data sensitivity, data volume, availability requirements, and others [S1]. Update and review classifications annually, or when significant enterprise changes occur [S1].

Leverage vetted modules or services for application security components, such as identity management, encryption, auditing, and logging, to minimize design or implementation errors [S1]. Modern operating systems provide effective mechanisms for identification, authentication, and authorization [S1]. Use only standardized, currently accepted, and extensively reviewed encryption algorithms [S1].

Conduct post-incident reviews to identify lessons learned and follow-up actions to prevent security incident recurrence [S1]. This activity is captured by Safeguard 17.8: Conduct Post-Incident Reviews [S1]. Post-incident reviews help prevent incident recurrence through identifying lessons learned and follow-up actions [S1].

Validate security measures after every penetration test, and update detection rules when necessary [S1]. If deemed necessary, modify rulesets and capabilities to detect techniques used during testing [S1]. This is in line with safeguard 18.4 [S1].
